sentences.text: On The 8 th Of August, 2025
Misc .
Civil Case No. 1046 of 2022

Arvind Patel
 Versus
 Chandrabhan Kaurav And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Sharad Gupta - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Vikas Jyotishi - Advocate for the respondent No.
 Shri Krishna Namdeo - Advocate for respondent No.3.

Order 
Heard on I.A. No.3089/2025, which is an application for dispense with the service of respondent No.1.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the original Misc. Appeal No.2869/2019, no notice was issued to respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 was not represented at the time of dismissal of the application.
He further submits that though the notices were issued in the present M.C.C., but the same could not be served upon respondent No.1 and the present MCC is pending since 2022.
He further submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the service of respondent No.1 be dispensed with.
Respondent No.2 and 3 have no objection.
After consideration, application is allowed.

Service of respondent No.1 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37228 2 MCC-1046-2022 is hereby dispensed with.
Heard on I.A. No.4695/2022 for condonation of delay occurred in filing the present MCC.
As per office report, present MCC is barred by 903 days.

The applicant preferred the Misc. Appeal under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act assailing the award passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in favour of respondent No.1 mainly on the ground of liability as the Tribunal has issued direction to recover the amount of compensation from the owner of the vehicle, after making payment to the claimant.

It is submitted on behalf of applicant that inadvertently the counsel for Arvind Patel vs Chandrabhan Kaurav on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157043454/
1 applicant could not check the status of the case and his Lawyer was not aware of regarding dismissal of Misc. Appeal for non-compliance of peremptory order and therefore, the restoration application could not be filed in time.
Counsel for the applicant prays for condoning the delay occurred in filing the present M.C.C.
Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 and 3 opposed the application and submits that no sufficient ground is made out for condoning the delay.
The application has been moved after inordinate delay.
After consideration, I deem it proper to allow the application filed under Section 5 of Limitation Act.
It appears that applicant has able to make out sufficient ground and to explain the delay occurred in filing the application.
Consequently, application is allowed.
Delay is hereby condoned.

Heard on main application filed for restoration of Misc. Appeal No.2869/2019, which was dismissed on 1.10.2019 due to non-compliance of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37228 3 MCC-1046-2022 common conditional order dated 13.8.2019.
Counsel for the applicant submits that inadvertently the defect could not be cured and application for condonation of delay could not be filed in original Misc. Appeal.

He submits that if the Misc.
Appeal is not restored, the applicant will be deprived from getting the order on merits.
He prays for restoration of Misc. Appeal.
Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 and 3 opposed the prayer and submit that no ground for restoration is made out as the applicant failed to comply with the common conditional order.
After consideration, the application is allowed.
M.A. No.2869/2019 is restored to its original number.
Office is directed to restore M.A. No.2869/2019 and place the same before the Roster Bench for consideration, subject to removal of the defects pointed out by the office.
Copy of this order be placed in M.A. No.2869/2019.
With the aforesaid, present M.C.C. is disposed of.
(VINAY SARAF) JUDGE irfan Arvind Patel vs Chandrabhan Kaurav on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157043454/
